main_text.p: p. 82. Βάκχε ἦτοι Μάκχα ἡ Μάκχ, Baccha, sive Make, aut Makech, habetur, quod idem προσκύνημα ἐπαρήματος, Adoramen observationis, vocatur pag. 14. & pag. 82. προσκυνητήριον, &c. Adoratorium observationis (quâ periphrasi Araḇum قبلة Keblah, locum scil. ad quem inter orandum faciem conuertunt, qui non alius quam Templum Meccanum est) & quod in priori loco ἐν τῷ ἐὐχῆς in posteriori ἐν τῷ εὐχῆς, Domus orationis, appellatur, quam ab Abrahamo & Ismaele structam fingunt. Sciendum ergò quid de كعبة dicant Arabes: esse scil. nomen τῆς كعبہ [?] Mecca, inde illi inditum quòd tanta sit illuc religionis prætextu confluentium turba, ut se mutuò impellant & premant, quæ inter cæteras verbi كعب notiones est, sunt qui loci proprie Becca dicti limites non ultra illum in quo προσκυνητήριον illud structum sit, proferant, quod extra illum est dici Mecca, testibus Ebnol Athir, Safioddin, &c. at Euthymius & alter ille utramque pro ipso oratorio ibi constructo quod ipsi Caabam vocant, sumpsisse videtur. Cui qui quantum detulerint & οἱ φρόδεν [?] Arabes & qui cis Mohammedem, honorem reputaverint,Aljauh. Ebn Athir. Kamus, aliam & afferunt rationem quod superba immorigerorum colla subigat et conterat.لابهاديكم اعـنـاں الجماعة non malè forsan illud ipsorum εἴδωλον dixerit. εἰδωλὸν olim fuisse vidimus, locum jam autumant Deo in terris unicè charum( quemque ipsi sacrum habent, adeo ut non alias quam facie ad eam versâ effusas preces, Deo acceptas credant. de ea, cujus memi-nit, fabulâ, quâ domus illa ab Abrahamo & Ismaele structa perhibetur, plura mox ubi priùs de lapide τῷ Βέκχᾳ[?] pauca. Ebnol Athir.Quomodo (inquit) vos lapidi adhæ-retis Brathhan, & ipsum osculamini? Lapidem describere videtur istum, quem osculari Meccam religionis ergo visentibus, & Caabam circum euntibus, cul-Idolum olim ibi cultum, & jam in eo occultum seu sepultum manere, credi à Judæis patet ex Epistola Maimonidis prædicta.

page.notes: The right margin has an italic note column (Arabic words in the lowest part) which is set beside the text; reading is uncertain in places. Greek and Arabic words marked [?] are doubtful. The first line's Greek, and the Greek within the lines, are uncertain. The page number is printed in old-style numerals as "ııʒ", read here as 113. Printed paragraph division is not clear in the scan; the text is kept as one paragraph. The Arabic note at the top right is only partly legible and is not transcribed; the first Greek word after "ipsorum" and the Greek name "τῷ Βέκχᾳ" are doubtful. The Arabic note is not transcribed. The notes "Ebnol Athir." and the long note beside the lines are placed at the point where they stand. The page number and running head are not printed on this part.
